**Good to know:** use the item `code` in your data, not the label. Codes stay the same when a label is reworded.

GET /api/vod/:id/delete-impact.summary: What deleting an asset would take
GET /api/vod/:id/delete-impact.description: Before deleting: the asset's title (`name`, typed to confirm in the console), its availability, what goes with it (`counts`: skip markers, social formats, reviews, portal and app publishing points), the social posts that stay on their platforms (`counts.social_posts`), how many days the restore bin keeps it (`binDays`) and `blocker`, why the delete would be refused now (it is in the active lineup of a FAST channel, named in `fastChannels`). Needs `vod: view`.

DELETE /api/vod/:id.summary: Delete an asset (into the restore bin)
DELETE /api/vod/:id.description: Removes the asset's record, metadata and media files from the library. Nothing is destroyed yet: it goes to the restore bin (Storage > Recently removed) for `binDays` days, until `purgeAfter`, and `POST /api/vod/{id}/restore` puts it back. Posts already on social platforms are not taken down. Refused (400) while the asset is in an active FAST lineup; `GET /api/vod/{id}/delete-impact` says so first. Needs `vod: manage`.

POST /api/vod/:id/restore.description: Puts an asset deleted with `DELETE /api/vod/{id}` back from the restore bin, with its metadata, markers and media files, under the same id. Needs `vod: manage`, the same as the delete. 404 when the asset is not in the bin (never deleted, already restored, or purged).

GET /api/vod.description: The account's on-demand library: recordings published as VOD, clips, uploads and watch-folder files. Search titles and file names with `q`, filter on any field below (for example `review_state=in_review` or `published=true`), and sort with `sort=-created_at`. Each asset carries its public status (`public_status`: draft, in_review, changes_requested, rejected, processing, scheduled, available, restricted, expired or archived), `status_reason`, the next moment it can change (`status_until`) and the editorial state people set (`editorial_state`: draft, published or archived); filter on them like any field (`public_status=restricted`), and `expires_within_days=7` keeps titles that are Available now and stop being available within that many days.

GET /api/recordings.description: Raw captures of live output, newest first. `q` searches titles and source names, then the programme on air and the transcript. Filter by `channel_id`, `kind`, `status` or time (`start_epoch_ms[gte]=...`).

GET /api/jobs/encode-queue.description: Your VOD encode jobs (`vod.encode`): `running` (with progress and the stage), `queued` in the order a worker will take them, each with its `position` in the platform's encode queue (1 is next; other accounts' encodes count, since the workers are shared), and `recent`, the last `recent` (default 50, at most 200) finished, failed or cancelled. Each names its asset (`asset_id`, `asset_title`) and source file. `platformBacklog` is every encode queued or running on the platform.

GET /api/jobs/:id/log.description: What the job printed, oldest first: `lines` of `{ seq, attempt, at, stream, line }`, where `stream` is `out` or `err` (the process), `step` (a stage the job announced) or `warn` (a step that failed without failing the job). Pass `after` (the last `seq` you have) to tail a running job; `last` is the seq to pass next. `limit` up to 5000 (default 1000). Progress lines are kept once per 5%, and a job keeps at most 4000 lines plus its last 200.

GET /api/jobs/:id/outputs.description: For a `vod.encode` job: each rendition and the audio (resolution, bitrate, codec, segments, bytes and a `state`: `ok`, `running`, `pending`, `failed`, `skipped` or `missing`), the HLS and DASH manifests, the thumbnails (candidate stills and the chosen image), the sprite sheets (sheets, previews, interval) and the jobs the encode queued after it (`followOn`). Read while the job runs too, from the files as they are written. 400 for other job types.

GET /api/jobs.description: Background work (encodes, imports, conversions) with its state. Typical: `state=failed,cancelled&created_at[gte]=2026-10-17` to find what went wrong today.

GET /api/timeline/grid.summary: Get the timeline grid (Past, Now, Next)
GET /api/timeline/grid.description:
Every stream the caller can see as one row on a shared clock, for the Live Streams Timeline view: programmes (as-run times preferred over scheduled), the media actually recorded with its gaps (past part of the window only, measured from disk), clip ticks, and the same five-gate status the Live board shows. One call for the whole grid instead of one per stream.

`from` and `to` are ISO 8601 (epoch ms also accepted); the window is capped at 48 hours and a wider one is a 400. `kinds` narrows to `channel,radio,event,loop` (rows of a kind your role cannot view are absent, not empty). Rows page at 50 with the list standard's cursor: follow `next` in the body or the `Link: rel="next"` header.

GET /api/account-settings/captions.description: The account's captions engine (`none`, `whisper` or `gladia`) and, for every output profile, whether it captions, the spoken language, the caption languages, the hold-back offset and the whisper model, with the groups and running streams that use it. Also says whether you may change the engine and the profiles, and which languages Volt can deliver.

PATCH /api/account-settings/captions.description: Set `provider` to `none` (captions off for every stream), `whisper` (self-hosted, no per-minute fee) or `gladia` (managed service). Account administrators and owners only. Refused with 409 `locked_while_running` while a stream with captions on is running, because the encoder reads it when a stream starts. Recorded in the audit log.

PATCH /api/account-settings/captions/pro.description: Any of `enabled`, `sourceLang` (`auto` or a language code), `targets` (languages from `GET /api/caption-languages`), `offsetSec` (0 to 60) and `modelSize` (`tiny`, `base`, `small`, `medium`, `large-v3`; whisper only). Applies to every channel, station and event in the groups that use the profile. Needs `settings: manage`. Refused with 409 `locked_while_running` while one of those streams is running. Recorded in the audit log.

PATCH /api/output-profiles/:id.summary: Turn trick-play on or off for an output profile
PATCH /api/output-profiles/:id.description: Set `trickPlay` to `true` or `false`: I-frame playlists for the players that scrub and fast-forward with them (AVPlayer on iOS, iPadOS, tvOS and Safari, many smart-TV players). Off by default. On, every on-demand asset made with the profile lists an `EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF` per video rendition in its HLS master, pointing at `<media playlist>.iframes.m3u8` beside the rendition's media playlist (byte ranges into the segments it already has), and its DASH MPD gains a trick-mode AdaptationSet per video set (`EssentialProperty` `http://dashif.org/guidelines/trickmode`) whose segments are its keyframes, each made when asked for from the same segments. Both are made within a few minutes and without a re-encode; encrypted assets keep their keys. Off, they are no longer listed or served. A clip follows its channel's or event's group profile; an upload follows the live profile its encoding ladder mirrors, else the account default. Account administrators and owners only. Recorded in the audit log.

GET /api/fast/channels/:id/ad-report.summary: How a FAST channel's breaks were filled and reported
GET /api/fast/channels/:id/ad-report.description: Over the last `days` (default 7, at most 90): decisions, paid fill, house and slate shares, ad server timeouts and errors, p95 answer time, the creatives offered, and `beacons`: what Volt reported to the ad servers for stitched breaks. Per event (`impression`, `start`, `firstQuartile`, `midpoint`, `thirdQuartile`, `complete`, VAST 4 `progress@` offsets) the number of ads that reached it and the tracking URLs answered (`sent`) or not (`failed`), with `impressions`, `completes` and `completionRate`. Beacons are sent server-side as each viewer's player reaches the moment, so a viewer who leaves halfway gives no complete.

GET /api/fast/channels/:id/breaks/:bid/b.summary: What was reported to the ad server for one break
GET /api/fast/channels/:id/breaks/:bid/b.description: For one break on a stitched FAST channel: per paid ad in the pod (`podIndex`, counting house spots and slate), per beacon event, how many viewer sessions reached it and how many tracking URLs were answered or failed; plus the latest 100 beacons with the tracker's host, its HTTP status and any error. A URL is sent once per viewer, never retried.

GET /live/:id/v/:key/:file.summary: Play the version of a live stream your viewer's rights give them
GET /live/:id/v/:key/:file.description:
Where `GET /live/{id}/master.m3u8` (or `manifest.mpd`) sends a viewer whose country, or rights class, has the current programme replaced: the same stream with the channel's loop in place of the programme inside each replace window. `{key}` names the version; `{file}` is `master.m3u8`, `manifest.mpd` or one of the media playlists the master lists. You do not build this address yourself: follow the redirect.

Every viewer gets their own version whatever `{key}` says, so a version is never a way round a block (451). Outside a window the version is the normal stream. Expect 404 when the stream is off air and 503 when the loop has not been built for it.

GET /live/:id/steering.summary: Which delivery path a viewer's player should use
GET /live/:id/steering.description:
Content steering. When Volt delivers a stream over more than one path (for example two CDNs), `GET /live/{id}/master.m3u8` and `manifest.mpd` list every path and name this address as the steering server (HLS `EXT-X-CONTENT-STEERING`, DASH `ContentSteering`). The player asks it which path to use, and asks again every `TTL` seconds: the answer is the paths in order (`PATHWAY-PRIORITY`), per viewer country, with a path that is clearly worse for viewers in that country over the last ten minutes moved last. Players that support content steering (Shaka, which the Volt player uses, hls.js and dash.js) move at the next segment, without a stall.

You do not call this yourself: the player does. `f` is `hls` or `dash`; the player adds its current path and measured throughput (`_HLS_pathway` and `_HLS_throughput`, or the `_DASH_` pair). The answer is never cached. Expect 404 when the stream is delivered over one path only.

GET /api/social/x.summary: Whether X is on for the account
GET /api/social/x.description: X charges for its API per post and per read, so it is off for an account unless a system administrator switches it on (`enabled`, posts then go through the Volt deployment's X app) or the account adds its own X developer app (`ownApp`, X then bills the account directly). `allowed` is true when either is set. `ownApp` gives the client id only: the secret is never returned. `canSwitch` says whether the caller may change the switch, and `callbackUrl` is the address to register in an own X app.

PATCH /api/social/x.summary: Switch X on or off for the account
PATCH /api/social/x.description: Body `{"enabled": true}`. System administrators only (on a Volt the account runs itself, its owner). Recorded in the audit log. Turning X off keeps the linked X accounts: they are listed with `off: true` and nothing is posted to them or read from them until X is on again.

GET /api/social/media/:file.summary: The video Threads fetches for a post
GET /api/social/media/:file.description: Threads takes no upload: the publish job gives it this address and Threads fetches the file. Answers only with the job's signature (`exp`, `sig`) and until it expires; anything else is 404. Not for clients: Volt makes these links itself when it publishes to Threads.

GET /api/social/accounts/:id/publishing-.summary: Posts used of the platform's publishing limit
GET /api/social/accounts/:id/publishing-.description: For a platform with a publishing limit (Instagram and Threads: a set number of API posts in a moving 24 hours, read from Instagram's content_publishing_limit or Threads' threads_publishing_limit), how many posts this linked account has used (`used`), is allowed (`total`) and has left (`remaining`), over `windowHours`. `applies` is false for a platform without one. A sandbox account counts its own posts. Publishing to an account with none left is refused with 422.

GET /api/social/publish-image/:fileId/de.summary: The default post for an Image Library picture
GET /api/social/publish-image/:fileId/de.description: Per platform that posts pictures (Instagram, Threads), the post a picture gets by default: its name as the caption and its tags as hashtags.

POST /api/social/publish-image/:fileId.description: Publishes a picture from the Image Library as a feed post to the linked accounts in `targets`, each with its own `post`. Only platforms that post pictures are accepted (Instagram, Threads); another platform, a caption over its limits (Instagram: 2,200 characters, 30 hashtags; Threads: 500 characters, one hashtag) or an account at its publishing limit answers 422 with the reasons. Instagram and Threads fetch the picture themselves as a signed JPEG from the Volt's public address, so a Volt without one reachable from the internet fails the post with a message saying so. Returns the new publications, which move from pending to published or failed; list them with `GET /api/social/publications?imageId=`.

PUT /api/social/x/app.summary: Use the account's own X developer app
PUT /api/social/x/app.description: Body `{"clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "..."}` from an X app with OAuth 2.0 turned on and `callbackUrl` from `GET /api/social/x` registered in it. With its own app the account can use X without the platform switch, and X bills it directly. The secret is stored encrypted and never returned. Needs `settings: manage`. Recorded in the audit log by client id.

DELETE /api/social/x/app.summary: Stop using the account's own X app
DELETE /api/social/x/app.description: Forgets the client id and secret. Linked X accounts are kept; X turns off unless the platform switch is on for the account. Needs `settings: manage`.

GET /api/vod/ads/rules.description: The account default and each content type's own rule: whether titles get ads, where the breaks go (pre-roll, mid-rolls at cue points or every N minutes, post-roll), the ad server, the house spots, who plays ad-free and how ads reach the player.

PUT /api/vod/ads/rules/default.summary: Set the account's on-demand ad rule
PUT /api/vod/ads/rules/default.description: Body `{"mode": "on", "policy": {...}, "adServerId": "...", "houseAds": [{"assetId": "..."}]}`. `policy` takes `preroll`, `midroll`, `postroll`, `podMaxAds`, `maxAdSec`, `adFreeFor` (`entitlement`, `members`), `snapback`, `prerollOnResume` and `delivery` (`auto`, `stitched`, `guided`); values out of range are brought into range. New plays follow it at once. Recorded in the audit log.

PUT /api/vod/ads/rules/content-type/:id.summary: Set a content type's own on-demand ad rule
PUT /api/vod/ads/rules/content-type/:id.description: The same body as the account default. A title of this content type plays under this rule instead of the default; `mode: off` keeps the content type free of ads.

DELETE /api/vod/ads/rules/content-type/:.summary: Back to the account default for a content type

GET /api/vod/ads/assets/:id/plan.summary: Where a title's ad breaks would go
GET /api/vod/ads/assets/:id/plan.description: The rule the title plays under and its breaks (position, content time, planned length). Mid-rolls are moved to the nearest segment start. `why` says why there are none: no rule on, the title is marked `adRule: none`, or no break fits.

GET /api/vod/ads/report.description: For the last `days` (1 to 90, default 7), optionally one `assetId`: plays with ads, breaks, fill rate, house share, ad server timeouts and errors, impressions, completion rate, clicks and click rate.

POST /api/vod/ads/ad-servers.description: Body `{"name": "...", "vendor": "gam", "tagTemplate": "https://...", "timeoutMs": 1500}`. The VAST tag URL takes IAB macros such as `[CACHEBUSTING]`, `[BREAK_POSITION]` and `[CONTENT_ID]`.

GET /api/vod/ads/house-candidates.summary: Library items that can be house spots
GET /api/vod/ads/house-candidates.description: Items of two minutes or less with a playlist.

GET /vod-ads/s/:sid/timeline.json.description: For a stitched play (from the play gate's `ads.timelineUrl`): each break's place in the title (`contentSec`) and in the stream (`stitchedStartSec`), its length, its ads with `clickUrl`, `snapback`, and the `eventsUrl` for player events.

POST /vod-ads/s/:sid/events.summary: Report player events on an ad
POST /vod-ads/s/:sid/events.description: Body `{"events": [{"b": 1, "p": 0, "event": "pause"}]}`, `b` the break index and `p` the ad's place in it. Events: pause, resume, mute, unmute, rewind, fullscreen, exitFullscreen, playerExpand, playerCollapse, skip, closeLinear. Volt sends the ad's trackers for them. Impressions and quarters are sent by Volt itself.

GET /vod-ads/s/:sid/click/:b/:p.description: Open it in a new window when the viewer clicks an ad. Volt records the click, sends the ad's click trackers with the viewer's address and player, then redirects (302) to the advertiser's page. 404 when the ad has no page.

GET /vod-ads/s/:sid/manifest.mpd.description: For a stitched play, the play gate's `delivery.dash` when the title was encoded with DASH. The title's own Periods cut at each break, with a Period per ad between them (its segments through the session, so impressions and quartiles are sent for any player); captions continue with a blank WebVTT during ads; protection stays on the content and ads are clear. 404 when one of the ads decided for this viewer has no fMP4 rendition: play the session's HLS instead.

GET /vod-ads/s/:sid/text/:k/:rep.description: Named by the stitched MPD, `:rep` is `<Representation id>.vtt`: the title's sidecar WebVTT between Period `k`'s start and end, its cue times on that Period's clock.

GET /vod-ads/g/:assetId/:ver/list/:b.summary: One break's ads (HLS Interstitials asset list)
GET /vod-ads/g/:assetId/:ver/list/:b.description: Asked by the player when it reaches a break of a guided playlist, with `_HLS_primary_id` (or `sid`). Decided for that playback: `ASSETS` with each ad's `URI` and `DURATION`.

GET /fast/:id/s/:sid/ads.json.summary: The ads in a FAST viewer's breaks
GET /fast/:id/s/:sid/ads.json.description: The paid ads in the viewer's recent stitched breaks: when each plays (wall clock) and its `clickUrl`, for a player of your own.

GET /fast/:id/s/:sid/click/:bid/:p.summary: A click on a FAST ad
GET /fast/:id/s/:sid/click/:bid/:p.description: Records the click with the break's beacons, sends the ad's click trackers, then redirects (302) to the advertiser's page.

GET /api/public/epg/channels.description: Every channel with the guide turned on in the account the key belongs to: id, XMLTV id, name, number, icon, time zone and whether it plays a FAST lineup.

GET /api/public/epg/now.description: Previous, now and next for every guide channel, or the ones in `channels` (ids or XMLTV ids, comma separated). `previous` defaults to 0 and `next` to 1, each up to 20. `at` asks about another moment.

GET /api/public/epg/channels/:ref/now.summary: Previous, now and next on a channel
GET /api/public/epg/channels/:ref/now.description: `previous` (default 1) and `next` (default 3), each up to 20. `now` carries `progress`; `nextChangeAt` says when the answer next changes, which is when an app should ask again.

GET /api/public/epg/channels/:ref/schedu.description: A local day with `date=YYYY-MM-DD` (in `tz`, default the channel's zone), or a window with `from` and `to`, up to 14 days. Default: today in the channel's zone. `links.previous` and `links.next` page by the same length.

GET /api/public/epg/grid.description: Several channels over a window: `from` and `to`, or `hours` from the top of this hour (default 3), up to 48 hours. `channels` limits it to some channels.

GET /api/public/epg/programmes/:id.description: One programme with the programmes before and after it on the same channel.

GET /api/collections.description: Every collection of the account, flat and ordered for a tree, with direct and total item counts.

POST /api/collections.description: At the top level, or inside `parentId`.

GET /api/collections/:id.description: With its breadcrumb path and its sub-collections.

PATCH /api/collections/:id.description: Rename, describe, recolour, reorder, or move it (`parentId`). It can't move inside itself. Also takes `rules` (a tree: `{ match: all|any, conditions: [ {field, op, value} | group ] }`, or `null` to turn rules off) and `orderBy` (`manual`, `title`, `-created_at`, `-first_aired_at`, `-duration` and others from `GET /api/collections/rules/fields`). Saving rules matches the whole library at once.

DELETE /api/collections/:id.description: Removes it and its sub-collections. The media stays in the library.

GET /api/collections/:id/items.description: In the collection's order. `deep=true` adds the sub-collections' media after, each asset once.

POST /api/collections/:id/items.description: `assetIds` are appended in the order given. Duplicates and assets from other accounts are ignored.

POST /api/collections/:id/items/remove.description: The media stays in the library and in any other collections.

PUT /api/collections/:id/items/order.description: Every asset in the collection, once each, in the new order.

GET /api/collections/memberships.description: `assetIds` comma separated. Returns the collection ids for each asset.

GET /api/fast/channels/:id/rundown.description: What the playout plays next, to the second: programmes, ad breaks, idents and the brand loop. `hours` ahead (default 3), `back` hours behind.

POST /api/channels/:id/group.summary: Move a channel to another group
POST /api/channels/:id/group.description: `groupId` of another of the account's groups with the same workflow (transcode or packaging). Works for TV channels, radio stations and FAST channels; needs Manage on that kind. Refused (409) when the target group's share of the plan is full or its workflow differs. A running channel keeps running; the target group's output profile applies from its next start (`profileChanges`, `running` in the answer).

POST /api/events/:id/group.summary: Move an event to another group
POST /api/events/:id/group.description: `groupId` of another of the account's groups with the same workflow. An event that has not ended needs room in the target group's running at once for its scheduled window (409 otherwise). Needs Events: Manage.

PATCH /api/radio/:id/log/:entryId.description: Body `{ "class": "song" | "ad" | "content" }`. Only the class changes: the received ICY block and stream URL stay as they were. The answer has the new `class`, `classAuto` (what the classifier said, kept through later corrections) and `classBy` (who corrected it), and the log (`GET /api/radio/{id}/log`) returns `class_by` and `class_auto` on corrected entries. The class decides the log's counts, what is transcribed (content) and what gets a cover lookup (songs). Needs `radio: operate`. 404 for an entry that is not in this station's now-playing log; every change is in the audit log.

GET /api/radio/:id/delete-impact.description: The counts of what goes with the station (recordings, clips and how many are published, log and guide entries, scheduled clips, sources) and a `blocker` naming why it cannot be deleted yet (it is live, or its encoder is still running), else null.

DELETE /api/radio/:id.description: Removes the station with its recordings, clips, log and guide (the same as `DELETE /api/channels/{id}` for a station). Owners and administrators only (403 otherwise). Refused (400) while the station is live or its encoder still runs: stop it first. 404 for an id that is not one of your stations, a TV channel included. Answers 204; the deletion is in the audit log.

GET /api/recordings/sources.description: One row per channel, radio station or event with recorded content, with its counts, available range and live state. `q` matches the source's name, or a programme or song title that aired inside one of its recordings (guide entries and a station's now-playing log); a guide entry with no recording under it is not a match. With `q`, each row's `match` says why: `{ "by": "name" }`, or `{ "by": "aired", "title", "atMs", "count" }` naming the latest matching entry and how many matched. Also `type` (csv of channel, radio, event), `sort`, `dir`, `recordedFrom`/`recordedTo`, `createdFrom`/`createdTo` (epoch ms) and `recordingNow=1`.

GET /api/filler-assets/tags.summary: Tags in use on slates and loops
GET /api/filler-assets/tags.description: Every tag on a slate or loop in this account, with how many carry it: `[{ "tag": "Sport", "count": 4 }]`. Filter the list with `GET /api/filler-assets?tag=Sport` (a comma list means all of them).

PUT /api/filler-assets/:id/tags.summary: Set a slate or loop's tags
PUT /api/filler-assets/:id/tags.description: `{ "tags": ["Sport", "Brand A"] }` replaces its tags. Tags are trimmed, kept to 40 characters and 20 per item, and a tag that differs from another only in case is dropped.

GET /api/filler-assets/:id/house.summary: A slate or loop's house preview, QC and approval
GET /api/filler-assets/:id/house.description: `status` (queued, building, ready, failed) and `preview` (the HLS address in `preview.url`, which plays the loop three times over with a discontinuity between rounds; the house format used; the length played and the file's length); `qc` with `state` (pass, warnings, failed), `findings` (each with `check`, `severity`, `message`, `measured`, `expected` and where in the loop) and `skipped`; `review` (pending, approved, rejected, who, when, note); `availability` (available or archived).

POST /api/filler-assets/:id/house.summary: Build a slate or loop's house preview again
POST /api/filler-assets/:id/house.description: Queues the house preview and its QC again, for example after the account's output profiles change. 202. 409 while the file is still uploading.

POST /api/filler-assets/:id/qc.summary: Run QC again over a house preview
POST /api/filler-assets/:id/qc.description: Measures the existing house preview again and answers as `GET /api/filler-assets/{id}/house`.

POST /api/filler-assets/:id/review.summary: Approve or reject a slate or loop
POST /api/filler-assets/:id/review.description: `{ "decision": "approve" | "reject" | "reset", "note": "..." }`. Only an approved slate or loop can be newly given to a channel, station, event or FAST channel. Approving over a QC error, or with no house preview, needs a `note` (400 without). Rejecting does not take it off streams that already use it: the answer's `usedBy` names them. `reset` sends it back to waiting.

POST /api/filler-assets/:id/availability.summary: Archive a slate or loop, or make it available
POST /api/filler-assets/:id/availability.description: `{ "state": "archived" | "available" }`. An archived slate or loop is kept but cannot be newly given to anything and is left off the pickers. Refused (409, with `inUseBy`) while a channel, station, event or FAST channel uses it.

PUT /api/filler-assets/:id/poster.description: `{ "key": <a frame from poster_candidates> }` uses that frame; `{ "auto": true }` goes back to the best-scoring frame. A frame that is not one of this loop's is refused (404).

POST /api/filler-assets/:id/thumbnails.summary: Make a slate or loop's thumbnails again
POST /api/filler-assets/:id/thumbnails.description: Queues the thumbnail job again: the thumbnail, a loop's frames and sprite sheets, and the file's format (resolution, codecs, frame rate, bitrates) read again. A thumbnail chosen by hand is kept while that frame is made again. 409 while the file is still uploading.

GET /api/filler-assets/:id/thumbnails.vt.description: One cue per sprite tile, pointing into the loop's signed sprite sheets, for hover and scrub previews in a player. 404 for a slate (a still has no timeline) or a loop whose thumbnails are not made yet.

GET /api/vod/:id/frame-index.description: The frame rate, frame count, duration and first and last timecode of an asset's video, read from the rendition players get. `state` is `ready`, `none` (no video yet, or audio only; `note` says which) or `failed`. An asset with no index yet answers `{ "state": "queued" }` and one is made within seconds; `build=true` makes it now. Timecode is `HH:MM:SS:FF` at the asset's own rate, drop-frame (`HH:MM:SS;FF`) at 29.97 and 59.94 fps.

GET /api/vod/:id/frame.summary: Get one exact frame of an asset
GET /api/vod/:id/frame.description: Name the frame with `n` (frame number from 0), `tc` (timecode) or `ms` (the frame on screen at that time). Answers the frame number, its timecode and time, the segment that holds it and a signed image URL `w` pixels wide (default 640, up to 4096). The picture is the frame itself, decoded from the one segment that holds it, not the nearest keyframe. `redirect=true` answers 302 to the image instead, for use in an ``. 409 while the asset's frame index is being made, 404 for a frame outside the asset.

GET /api/recordings/:id/frame.summary: Get one exact frame of a recording
GET /api/recordings/:id/frame.description: Name the moment with `n` (frames from the recording's start), `ms` (time from the start) or `at` (wall clock, epoch ms). Answers the frame on screen at that moment: its number and timecode from the start, its wall-clock time, the capture segment that holds it and a signed image URL `w` pixels wide (default 640). `redirect=true` answers 302 to the image. 404 outside the recording or in a gap in the capture.

GET /api/sites.description: The account's sites, each with its `health` (healthy, degraded, offline, no_hosts or disabled, from its approved hosts only), host counts, the agent and encoder versions its hosts run and when one was last heard from. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/sites.description: A location of yours that will run the Volt site agent: `name` (unique in the account, ignoring case) and an optional `description`. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

GET /api/sites/:id.description: The site with `hostList` (each host's standing, health and the facts it last reported), its unused enrolment tokens by prefix (never in clear) and the heartbeat timings. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

PATCH /api/sites/:id.description: Rename, describe, or set `status` to `disabled` (its agents are refused) or `active`. Send the `version` you read to refuse a change made by someone else in between. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/sites/:id/enrolment-tokens.description: A one-time token for the site agent (`volt-agent site enrol <server> <token>`), valid for `expiresInHours` (default 24, at most 168). The token is in this answer only. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

DELETE /api/sites/:id/enrolment-tokens/:.description: An unused token stops working. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/sites/:id/hosts/:hostId/approv.description: The host may take work at this site. It learns of it on its next heartbeat. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/sites/:id/hosts/:hostId/reject.description: The host is refused and its credential stops working at once. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/sites/:id/hosts/:hostId/rotate.description: A new credential for the host, handed to its agent on the next heartbeat; the old one stops working the first time the new one is used. The new secret is never returned here. Needs the Hybrid Sites or the Mirror and Archive add-on: without either the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/watchfolders/:id/rules/default.summary: Add the default rules by file type
POST /api/watchfolders/:id/rules/default.description: Adds the default rules a watchfolder lacks (images to the Image Library, video to the Media Library; an on-prem folder gets the video rule only), after the folder's own rules, so nothing it does today changes for a file an existing rule already catches. A new folder starts with them unless it was created with `"defaultRules": false`; this is for folders made before them, or whose default was deleted. Answers 201 with `added` and the folder's `rules`, or 200 with an empty `added` when the folder has them all. Needs `media: manage`.

GET /api/watchfolders/site-options.description: What the New watchfolder form may offer for an on-prem folder: `licensed` (whether the account has the Hybrid Sites add-on), its `sites` (id, name, status) and the `placements` with whether each can be chosen yet (`upload_cloud` can; `encode_site` arrives with site encoders). An on-prem folder is then created with `POST /api/watchfolders` and `"kind": "site"`, `siteId`, `placement` and `config.path` (the folder's path on the site's server).

GET /api/rights/profiles.description: The account's rights profiles, the two built-ins (`builtin`: `open` for No restrictions, `closed` for All restricted) and its own, each with `assetCount` and `isDefault` (what new assets get). Every asset carries one profile: territories, apps, uses, access types and window. Nothing can show an asset outside its rights.

POST /api/rights/profiles.description: Territories (`territoryMode` `worldwide`, `allow` or `block` with `territories` as ISO country codes), apps (`appMode` `all`, `allow` or `block` with `appTypes` from `web`, `mobile`, `smart_tv`, `embed`, `partner`, `venue` and `appIds` naming registered apps), `uses` (`on_demand`, `fast`, `clips`, `social`, `downloads`, `ads`), `accessTypes` (`free`, `members`, `subscription`, `ppv`) and `window` (`open`, `fixed` with `from` and `until`, or `relative` with `count`, `unit` and `from`: `first_air` or `ingest`).

GET /api/rights/profiles/:id.description: One profile, with `assetCount`, `isDefault` and `setBy` (how its assets got it: watchfolder, chosen at upload, account default, set or bulk by a person).

PUT /api/rights/profiles/:id.description: Replaces the profile's settings (same body as create). Built-in profiles cannot be changed (409). Every asset on the profile follows the change at once: the play gate, publishing and FAST read it straight away.

DELETE /api/rights/profiles/:id.description: Only a profile no asset uses and that is not the default for new assets (409 otherwise). Built-ins cannot be deleted.

GET /api/rights/profiles/:id/assets.description: The assets that carry the profile, newest assignment first, with whether each is narrowed. `limit` (up to 500) and `offset`.

PUT /api/rights/agreements/:id.description: The file's bytes as the body (up to 25 MB), its name in `name`. Stored privately, never public. Replaces the one before.

GET /api/rights/agreements/:id.description: Needs Rights: Manage. Every download is written to the audit log.

GET /api/rights/settings.description: `defaultProfileId` (what an asset gets when its upload, watchfolder or API call names no profile) and the ids of the two built-ins.

GET /api/rights/assets/:id.description: Its `profile`, its own `narrow`ing, how it got them, and the `effective` rights (the profile with the narrowing applied).

PUT /api/rights/assets/:id.description: `{ "profileId", "narrow" }`. `narrow` can only take away: `territories` (only these), `blockTerritories`, `appTypes` (only these), `blockAppIds`, `uses` (only these), `from`, `until`. A narrowing wider than the profile is refused with 422 and the reasons in `problems`.

POST /api/rights/assign.summary: Assign a rights profile in bulk
POST /api/rights/assign.description: `{ "profileId", "assetIds": [...] }`, up to 1,000. Assets of another account are skipped. Per-title narrowing is cleared unless `keepNarrowing` is true.

POST /api/rights/check.description: `{ "assetId", "country", "appId" or "appType", "use", "at" }`: what the rights alone answer (`allowed`, and `code` `territory`, `app`, `use` or `window` with a `reason`). Collection access and the publishing policy decide inside this; the play gate gives the full answer.

GET /api/archive/targets.description: The account's Mirror and Archive storage targets: folders at one of its sites (on the site's server or a mounted NAS share) where the site agent keeps extra copies. Each has its `siteId`, `kind` (`path`: a folder; `s3`: an S3-compatible store at the site, with its `s3` settings: `endpoint`, `bucket`, `prefix`, `region`, `pathStyle`, `credentialRef`, never keys), `path` on the site's server (for a store, the bucket and the folder in it), optional `bandwidthMbps` cap, `recheckDays` (how often its verified copies are read back again; null: only when asked), `mirrorGraceDays` (how long a copy made under a mirror-mode rule stays after its asset left Volt for good, 0 to 90, 7 by default), `pendingDeletes` and `nextDeleteAt` (mirror deletes waiting at it) and `status`. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on: without it the answer is 403 with the code `licence_required`. Account administrators (owner or admin) only.

POST /api/archive/targets.description: `name` (unique in the account, ignoring case), `siteId` (one of your sites), `path` (an absolute folder on the site's server, such as `/mnt/nas/archive`, `D:\\Archive` or `\\\\nas\\archive`; no `.` or `..` segments) an optional `bandwidthMbps` (1 to 100000; copies never go faster) and an optional `recheckDays` (how often verified copies are read back again, 1 to 3650 days; 30 when not given, null for no scheduled re-checks) and an optional `mirrorGraceDays` (0 to 90, 7 when not given). For an S3-compatible store at the site (MinIO, NetApp StorageGRID and similar) send `kind` `s3` and `s3`: `endpoint` (`http(s)://host[:port]` as the site's server reaches it, no path), `bucket`, optional `prefix` (the folder in the bucket), `region` (default `us-east-1`), `pathStyle` (default true) and `credentialRef` (the name of the keys on the agent host, default `default`). Keys are never accepted: a request carrying `secretAccessKey`, `accessKeyId` or similar answers 400 `keys_stay_at_site`. Any other kind answers 422 `kind_not_available`. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

GET /api/archive/targets/:id.description: One storage target of the account. Another account's target answers 404. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

PATCH /api/archive/targets/:id.description: Change `name`, `path`, `bandwidthMbps` (null for no cap), `recheckDays` (null for no scheduled re-checks), `mirrorGraceDays` (0 to 90; deletes already waiting move by the difference) or `status` (`active`, or `disabled`: no new copies are queued to it; copies already there are kept). For a store target change `s3` instead of `path` (fields not sent are kept; keys are refused with 400 `keys_stay_at_site`). A target keeps its kind. A target that already holds copies keeps its folder, store, bucket and prefix: changing them answers 409 `target_in_use`; its `credentialRef` and `region` can still change. The answer lists what `changed`. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

GET /api/archive/copies.description: Every copy made to the account's storage targets, newest first; filter by `target_id`, `vod_asset_id` or `state`. `state` is `queued` (shown as `copying` while a site host runs it), `verified` (read back from the target and matched to the original's checksum), `failed` (no attempts left; `error` says why), `corrupt` (a re-check found it changed), `missing` (a re-check found it gone) or `removed` (a mirror-mode copy the site agent deleted after its asset left Volt and the grace period passed; `removedAt`). `mode` is `archive` (never deleted by Volt) or `mirror`; `deleteAfter` is when a mirror copy may be deleted, empty while its asset is still in Volt or its restore bin. `verifiedAt` is when it was last confirmed. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

POST /api/archive/copies.summary: Copy an asset's original to a storage target
POST /api/archive/copies.description: `targetId` and `vodAssetId`: the asset's original file is copied by the site agent into the target's folder (named after the original, spaces and unsupported characters removed, `-2`, `-3` added if the name is taken) and counts only once the checksum read back from the target matches the original's. 202 with the queued copy; asking again for a copy that is queued or verified answers 200 with it; one that failed, changed or went missing is copied afresh. 422 `no_source` when the asset keeps no original; 409 `target_disabled` or `site_disabled`. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

GET /api/archive/copies/:id.description: One archive copy: target, asset, `storedPath` in the target's folder, `bytes`, `sha256`, `state`, `error`, and when it was copied, last verified and last checked. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

POST /api/archive/copies/:id/verify.description: Queues a re-check: the site agent reads the copy back from the target. The same checksum keeps it `verified` with a new `verifiedAt`; a different one makes it `corrupt`, a file that is gone `missing`. 202 when queued, 200 when a check is already waiting; 409 `not_copied` for a copy that was never made. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

PUT /api/storage/retention.summary: Create or change a retention rule
PUT /api/storage/retention.description: `name` and `stages` (each `afterDays` and `action`: `keep`, `to_cold`, `to_archive` or `delete`, with an optional `targetTier`), scoped to the account, a `channelId` or an `eventId`; `ruleId` changes an existing rule. `appliesTo` (`recording`, `asset` or `both`) and `enabled` are kept when not sent. `originalAfterDays` removes an asset's original file from the cloud that many days after it landed, and only once a verified archive copy of it is held at one of the account's storage targets (the renditions stay, so the title keeps playing); `null` keeps originals, not sending it keeps the rule's setting, and it needs the Mirror and Archive add-on (403 `licence_required`). `includeUploads` makes an account rule reach uploads and watch folder files too: on for a rule created now, off for rules made before it existed until it is turned on. A ladder this storage cannot carry out is refused with 400 and the reason.

GET /api/archive/originals.summary: List originals out of the cloud, or waiting
GET /api/archive/originals.description: Assets whose original a retention rule removed from the cloud (`state` `removed`: the archive copy named in `copy` is verified, and the renditions still play) or whose rule is due while the original waits for its archive copy (`state` `waiting`, with `waitCode` and `why`). `waitCode` is `no_copy`, `copy_pending`, `copy_failed`, `copy_corrupt`, `copy_missing`, `copy_stale` (the copy is of an earlier original), `copy_unchecked` (the copy could not be compared with the original's checksum), `in_use` (a job is reading the original), `no_licence` or `not_removable`. Filter by `state` or `wait_code`. Set the rule with `originalAfterDays` on `PUT /api/storage/retention`. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

POST /api/archive/originals/:assetId/res.summary: Restore an original to the cloud
POST /api/archive/originals/:assetId/res.description: Brings back an original a retention rule removed, from the verified archive copy it was removed against: a server at the copy's site reads the copy, checks it against the archived checksum and uploads it, and Volt reads back what arrived before the asset uses it again (at its old address). 202 with the asset's status (`restoring` true) when queued; 200 when a restore is already in flight. 409 `not_removed` when the original is in the cloud, `copy_not_verified` when the copy is missing, corrupt or failed, `target_disabled` or `site_disabled`; 422 `not_restorable` when its old address is not one Volt writes originals to. A failed attempt is retried; the reason of the last one is `restoreError` on the status and in `GET /api/archive/originals`. A restored original's retention clock restarts at the restore. Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on and a site agent of 0.12.0 or later.

GET /api/archive/originals/:assetId.description: What retention will do with one asset's original: `state` `none` (no original kept), `kept` (no rule removes it), `scheduled` (with `dueAt` and the `rule` that decides, at channel, event or account scope), `waiting` (due, with `code` and `message` saying why it stays) or `removed` (with `removedAt`, the archive `copy` it can come back from, `restorable`, `restoring` and the last `restoreError`). Needs the Mirror and Archive add-on.

GET /api/collections/rules/fields.description: The fields a collection rule can test (title, genre, tags, length, content type, rights profile, provider, dates, and the account's content type fields as `meta:<key>`), each with its type; the operators for each type; the choices for lists and references; and the orders a collection can have.

POST /api/collections/rules/preview.description: `{ "rules" }`: how many of the account's titles the rules match now (`count`), with a few of them (`sample`). Nothing is saved.

POST /api/collections/:id/recheck.description: Matches the rules over the whole library at once and returns what was `added` and `removed`. Rules also run within seconds of any title changing, and in full every night.

GET /api/collections/:id/exclusions.summary: Titles left out of a rule collection
GET /api/collections/:id/exclusions.description: What people took out of a rule collection. The rules leave these out until they are let back in.

POST /api/collections/:id/exclusions/rem.description: `{ "assetIds" }`: removes them from the left-out list and lets the rules decide again at once.

GET /api/vod/:id/finder.summary: Which Find details an asset uses
GET /api/vod/:id/finder.description: The finder for the asset's content type: `song` (Songs and Music videos use the song service: `POST /api/vod/{id}/song/find`) or `general` (every other type: `POST /api/vod/{id}/details/find`), the default search `term` (the type's title field, else the asset title) and, for the song finder, `song` (artist and title). Needs `vod: view`.

GET /api/vod/:id/schema.org.description: The asset as a schema.org `VideoObject` (a `Clip` for a clip) for search engines and partners: name, description, duration, thumbnail, publications, view count and `embedUrl`, the title's watch page, always. The plain media addresses (`contentUrl`, the MP4, and `associatedMedia`, HLS, DASH and MP4) carry no play token, so they are only included where they would not go round the play gate: for a token-free title, and, where play tokens are not enforced, for a title with no viewer condition (no country limit, rights territories or apps, payment, sign-in, DRM, allowed referrer domains or streams limit). Every other title has neither. Needs `vod: view`.

POST /api/vod/:id/details/find.description: Searches Wikidata for `q` (default: the title field's value) and maps each item onto the asset's content type fields through their schema.org names (`proposed`, field key to value, shaped to the field type), with the asset's `current` metadata, provenance and fields to compare, and `unmapped`, the fields this finder cannot fill. Saves nothing. Answers `200` with `error` set when Wikidata cannot be reached, `400` when the asset has no content type, `409` when the type uses the song finder. Needs `vod: manage`.

POST /api/vod/:id/details/use.description: Writes exactly the `values` given (field key to value, the ones a person ticked), checked as a metadata save checks them (`422` for a field the type does not have or a value that does not fit). `source` is `wikidata` (with `itemId`) or `page` (with `link`, the page read by `details/page`). An image found on the web is copied into the Image Library and the field holds the library reference. Each written field's `metadata_provenance` records `source`, `item` (Wikidata) or `site` (a page), `link`, who chose it, when, and the value it replaced (`was`). Audited. Needs `vod: manage`.

POST /api/vod/:id/details/page.description: Reads the one page at `url` (fetched once, like a link preview; private network addresses refused with `400`) for the schema.org JSON-LD and Open Graph details it publishes about its subject, and maps them onto the asset's content type fields through their schema.org names. `result` is shaped like a `details/find` result (`label`, `description`, `kinds`, `link`, `site`, `likely`, `proposed`, and `from`, where each proposed value came from: `json-ld`, `og` or `title`), with `current` and `unmapped` as there. A pasted image address proposes the image fields only. Saves nothing. Answers `200` with `error` set and `result: null` when the site refuses programs (`blocked: true`), the page cannot be read, or it publishes no details; `400` when the asset has no content type; `409` when the type uses the song finder. Needs `vod: manage`.

GET /api/vod/:id.description: The asset with its metadata, content type and publications. Its public status is computed at the moment you ask: `public_status`, `status_reason`, `status_until` (the next moment it can change on its own), `editorial_state` (draft, published or archived), `effective_from` and `effective_until` (the publish window inside the rights window), `listed_from` and `unlisted`, `archived_at`, and whether a public route shows it now (`publicly_visible`) and lists it in browse and search (`publicly_listed`). With play tokens on (VOLT_EDGE_TOKENS issue or enforce), `preview` holds the asset's addresses with a play token for previewing it in the console at any status (`hls`, `dash`, `progressive`, `mp3`, `m4a`, `expiresAt`); null when tokens are off. Needs `vod: view`.

PUT /api/vod/:id/availability.summary: Set when an asset is listed
PUT /api/vod/:id/availability.description: Body: `listedFrom` (ISO date and time, or `null` for the default, the start of its window) and `unlisted` (true: playable by link only, never in browse or search). Leave a field out to keep it. A Scheduled title past its Listed from date is a teaser on public routes: what it is and when, never a playable address. Nothing is reprocessed; the status is stored again at once and the change is audited. Answers with the new status fields as on `GET /api/vod/:id`. Needs `vod: manage`.

POST /api/vod/:id/archive.description: Takes the title off the catalogue and stops it playing; the media is kept and it can be restored at any time until retention removes it. Its publications are withdrawn and play tokens already handed out stop at the edge. Optional body `reason`. Audited. 409 when it is already archived. Needs `vod: operate`.

POST /api/vod/:id/unarchive.description: Body `to`: `draft` (the default; its dates are kept) or `published` (publishes it again through its rules, with every gate and the rights checked). If publishing refuses, the title is out of the archive as a draft and the answer is 409 with the reason. Audited. 409 `not_archived` when it is not archived. Needs `vod: operate`.

POST /api/vod/:id/evaluate.summary: Who can watch: test an asset
POST /api/vod/:id/evaluate.description: The play gate's own decision for one viewer, without a player. Body: `country` (two letters), `viewer` (`anonymous`, `signed_in` or `entitled`, a viewer whose purchase covers the title), `at` (an ISO date and time; default now) and optionally `appId`. Answers `outcome` (play, teaser, not_found, paywall, sign_in or blocked), `http` (the status the gate would answer: 200, 403, 402, 404 or 451), `message`, `decidedBy` (status, account, rights, on_demand, rules or none), `reason`, `ruleId`, the public `status` at that moment and `notChecked` (the player's page address and a real viewer's purchases). Changes nothing. Needs `vod: view`.

POST /api/public/availability.summary: Play gate: may this viewer play this asset
POST /api/public/availability.description: The answer for one viewer: 200 with a playback token and the addresses to play (on-demand addresses carry a play token in the path, `/t/<token>/...`, which the CDN checks on every manifest and segment request); 402 (`mode: paywall`, with `products` or `packages`) or 403 (`mode: sign_in` or `blocked`) with what would let them in and `message`; 451 (`mode: blocked`) where the region or the rights say no, with `code` (`region` or `rights`), `message` (the account's block message, default "Not available in your region") and `notify` (true when the account offers Notify me; see `POST /api/public/availability/notify`). An on-demand title that is not public (draft, in review, processing, restricted, expired or archived) is answered exactly as an unknown id: 404. A Scheduled title past its Listed from date is a teaser: 403 with `mode: scheduled`, `until` (when it becomes available; `availableFrom` is the same date for older players), `message`, `notify` and `meta` (title, description and artwork), never a token or an address.

GET /api/public/availability.description: The same decision as POST for a viewer who is not signed in, with `appKey`, `assetId` and optionally `geo` in the query, so the edge can cache it. A Scheduled title past its Listed from date answers 403 `mode: scheduled` with `until`, and the edge keeps that answer no longer than until the title opens.

POST /api/public/availability/notify.summary: Notify me when a title becomes available
POST /api/public/availability/notify.description: Body: `appKey`, `assetId`, optionally `geo` and `email`. Kept only when the play gate refuses this viewer right now with a 451 (region or rights) or a Scheduled teaser and the account offers Notify me (the gate's `notify: true`); the same decision is run, so it reveals nothing the gate would not. A signed-in viewer (viewer session in `Authorization`) is remembered by their id, anyone else by `email`; asking twice for the same title changes nothing. Answers 201 (or 200 when already asked) with `notify`, `created` and `reason` (`scheduled`, `region` or `rights`). 404 as the gate for an unknown or unpublished title; 409 when the title plays for this viewer or Notify me is not offered; 400 with neither a session nor an email. At most 30 an hour from one address.

GET /api/analytics/rights-demand.summary: Rights demand: who was refused where
GET /api/analytics/rights-demand.description: Viewers the play gate refused for a region or the rights (and play tokens the CDN refused from another country), by title and country, beside the plays where the title is licensed; unique viewers are counted from hashed viewer keys, never addresses. Read from daily rollups, up to a minute behind. Query: `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-DD; default the last 30 days, at most 400), `assetId`, `country`, `kind` (`vod`, `channel` or `event`), `limit` (titles, default 50, at most 200) and `format=csv` for a spreadsheet by title and country.

GET /api/billing.summary: Billing: this month so far and recent invoices
GET /api/billing.description: What Volt charges this account. `mode` is the deployment's billing (`off`: nothing is charged or invoiced; `contract`: invoices are issued and settled outside Volt; `automated`: invoices are charged to the card on file). `handling` is how this account's invoices are settled (`automated` or `contract`). `currentMonth` is the open month worked out so far (plan fee, server time at the current price, charges and credits), with `subtotalUsd`, `taxUsd` and `totalUsd`; it is null when billing is off. `invoices` is the latest twelve. All amounts are US dollars. Needs Account settings: View.

GET /api/billing/invoices.description: Every invoice of the account, newest month first, with the list standard (filter on `status` and `number`, sort, paging). One invoice per calendar month (UTC), issued on the 1st for the month before. `status`: `issued`, `paid`, `failed` or `void`.

GET /api/billing/invoices/:id.description: One invoice with its lines: each line's `source` (`plan`, `usage`, `addon`, `addon_pack` or `manual`), description, quantity, unit, unit price and amount, then subtotal, tax rate, tax and total. A line is never changed once issued; a correction appears as its own line (a credit) on a later invoice.

GET /api/billing/invoices/:id/csv.description: The invoice's lines as CSV (`text/csv`), one row per line, then Subtotal, Tax and Total rows, for your accounts team or a spreadsheet.

GET /api/billing/invoices/:id/pdf.description: The invoice as a PDF (`application/pdf`, A4): who it is billed to, the period, how it is settled, its status, every line, then subtotal, tax and total.
